article_title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
citation: Navarrete, E., Nehring, A., Schanze, S., Ewerth, R., & Hoppe, A. (2025). A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness. Int J Artif Intell Educ. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-025-00481-x
title: Eight-category taxonomy of video characteristics and contextual aspects for video-based learning
description: The review derives a taxonomy that organizes video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: audio features, visual features, textual features, instructor behavior, learners' activities, interactive features, production style, and instructional design. Each category is populated with sub-categories and example features drawn from the 257 reviewed articles, such as transcripts, metadata, and on-screen text under textual features, and quizzes, annotations, and navigation interface elements under interactive features. The authors state the taxonomy "provides a holistic view and allows to systematically consider the critical components of a learning video" and can support assessment, optimization, and customization of educational video content.
requirements: Articles must concern video-based learning materials with specific video characteristics that can be classified into the taxonomy's categories
constraints: Derived from computer science databases for the period 2016 to 2021, excluding work influenced by large language models and generative AI that emerged after the review period
target_learners: Researchers and designers of video-based learning environments and intelligent educational systems
target_learning_goals: Systematic consideration of video characteristics when designing, assessing, or customizing learning videos
examples: Table 3 of the review lists sub-categories per category, e.g. audio records and representation cues under audio features, and Khan-style, dialogue-style, and slide-based videos under production style
key_sources: Navarrete, E., Nehring, A., Schanze, S., Ewerth, R., & Hoppe, A. (2025). A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness. article_title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
citation: Navarrete, E., Nehring, A., Schanze, S., Ewerth, R., & Hoppe, A. (2025). A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness. Int J Artif Intell Educ. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-025-00481-x
title: Tools supporting video-based learning: information extraction, interactive tools, recommenders, classifiers, and navigation/segmentation tools
description: The review identifies eight types of tools and methods supporting video-based learning: information extraction methods, interactive tools, recommendation systems, classifiers and predictors, video navigation and segmentation tools, video analysis tools and methods, video summarization, and others. The review states "The first five tool types amount to 80% of the reviewed papers". Tools commonly exploit textual and visual features, using low-level tasks such as optical character recognition, keyword extraction, natural language processing, word embeddings, slide transition detection, and speech recognition to generate transcripts.
requirements: Tools typically rely on extracted video elements such as transcripts, video frames, images, and metadata as input
constraints: Coverage limited to computer science databases and the 2016–2021 period; excludes post-2021 generative AI developments
target_learners: Learners using educational videos in formal or informal settings
target_learning_goals: Improved access, navigation, recommendation, and support for learning with videos
examples: Interactive tools include in-video annotations, in-video quizzes, and feedback mechanisms to prevent mind wandering, such as systems that detect distraction and pause the video

Int J Artif Intell Educ. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-025-00481-x
title: Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning as the evidence-based framework underlying effective video design
description: The review situates video-based learning design within the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, which it describes as an evidence-based framework explaining how learners process information from videos and identifying principles for optimizing cognitive load. The review reports that research applying this framework established that "videos incorporating principles such as segmentation, coherence, and signaling, signiﬁcantly outperform those lacking these design elements". It also notes frameworks addressing motivational aspects and social presence have further refined understanding of effective educational videos, and states these theoretical foundations inform the technological features examined in the review.
requirements: Video design decisions should be grounded in the framework's principles for optimizing cognitive load
constraints: The review attributes these findings to prior work (e.g., Mautone & Mayer; Moreno & Mayer; Mayer et al.) rather than testing them itself
target_learners: Learners watching educational videos across formal and informal settings
target_learning_goals: Effective design of learning videos that manages cognitive load and supports knowledge retention
examples: The review cites segmentation, coherence, and signaling as multimedia learning principles that videos incorporating significantly outperform videos lacking

article_title: Effects of Voice-Based Synthetic Assistant on Performance of Emergency Care Provider in Training
citation: Damacharla, P., Dhakal, P., Stumbo, S., Javaid, A. Y., Ganapathy, S., Malek, D. A., Hodge, D. C., & Devabhaktuni, V. (2018). Effects of Voice-Based Synthetic Assistant on Performance of Emergency Care Provider in Training. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-018-0166-3
title: Voice-Based Synthetic Assistant (VBSA): a cloud-based Alexa-powered pedagogical agent for real-time monitoring and error correction in emergency care training
description: The VBSA is a task-specific, voice-only synthetic assistant built on the AWS cloud using Alexa Voice Service, DynamoDB, and Lambda. It monitors each step of a trainee's treatment process in real time, creates error variables when a mistake occurs, and speaks corrective recommendations back to the trainee, while a web-based dashboard lets one trainer monitor all trainees simultaneously. The article describes it as "a pedagogical agent without a computer avatar, effectively a scaled-down version," and reports that it was developed for the full MARCHE protocol though tested only on the massive hemorrhage scenario. Its architecture comprises nine functional blocks including interface, process monitoring, goal recognition, and dynamic task allocation.
requirements: Voice interaction without hindering the ECP's motor skills while treating the patient
Cloud connectivity; loss of internet makes the service unavailable for training
Trainee speech within a scripted vocabulary; participants passed an English accent proficiency screening
constraints: Tested only on the narrow massive hemorrhage scenario
Cannot distinguish error types corresponding to tourniquet application
Deployment in current form is not recommended due to lack of large-sample studies
target_learners: novice emergency care provider (ECP) trainees with little or no medical knowledge
target_learning_goals: executing the massive hemorrhage treatment procedure (MARCHE protocol) accurately and quickly
reducing implementation and reporting errors during treatment
examples: A paramedic trainee treating a manikin leg with massive hemorrhage interacted with the VBSA via Amazon Echo, initiating commands such as 'Alexa, ask assistant'
key_sources: Damacharla, P., Dhakal, P., Stumbo, S., Javaid, A. Y., Ganapathy, S., Malek, D. A., Hodge, D. C., & Devabhaktuni, V. (2018). Effects of Voice-Based Synthetic Assistant on Performance of Emergency Care Provider in Training. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-018-0166-3

article_title: Developing Interactive Learning Media for School Level Mathematics through Open-Ended Approach Aided by Visual Basic Application for Excel
citation: Rohaeti, E.E., Bernard, M., & Primandhika, R.B. (2019). Developing interactive learning media for school level mathematics through open-ended approach aided by Visual Basic application for Excel. Journal on Mathematics Education, 10(1), 59-68. https://jme.ejournal.unsri.ac.id
title: Interactive mathematics learning media built with Visual Basic Application for Excel (command buttons, shapes, macros)
description: Visual Basic for Excel is described as "a programming language from Microsoft Excel that can utilize a mathematical function that set figural objects, called 'shape,' to be more interactive". Students built calculators and props using Command Buttons, Shapes from the INSERT menu, Assign Macro, the DEVELOPER tab, and aided cells (e.g., cells J3 and J5 to avoid subtraction errors where inputs like 9-6 were detected as dates). Student groups produced simple calculators, shape-based calculators, jarimatika (finger arithmetic) props, and the Wayang Golek Games Excel.
requirements: Students first understand prerequisite number concepts such as natural, odd, even and prime numbers, then receive basic knowledge of making a simple calculator
constraints: Student-built media showed flaws, e.g., a random button not correctly integrated with the Randomize function and shape size not changing when a value was entered
target_learning_goals: creating interactive mathematics learning media for elementary school topics such as numbers, operations, and geometry
examples: A first group made a simple calculator with Command Buttons; a second used Shapes with Assign Macro; a fourth group made jarimatika props; a sixth group made the WAGGE integer addition/subtraction game
key_sources: Rohaeti, E.E., Bernard, M., & Primandhika, R.B. (2019). Developing interactive learning media for school level mathematics through open-ended approach aided by Visual Basic application for Excel. Journal on Mathematics Education, 10(1), 59-68. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1204890

article_title: Understanding contexts and mechanisms through which video based benchmarking promotes alignment of examiners' scoring in objective structured clinical exams.
citation: Edwards, R. J., Yeates, P., Lefroy, J., & McKinley, R. (2025). Understanding contexts and mechanisms through which video based benchmarking promotes alignment of examiners' scoring in objective structured clinical exams. Advances in Health Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-025-10454-3
title: Middle-range realist theory of how video-based benchmarking aligns OSCE examiners' judgements
description: A middle-range programme theory built from 13 context-mechanism-outcome configurations (CMOCs) derived from realist interviews with 16 OSCE examiners. It holds that "examiners' expectations remain uncertain until encountering concrete performance examples", that judging a video and comparing with an expert standard lets examiners locate their judgement, that discrepancy produces dissonance resolved by adjustment or dismissal, and that degree of engagement with observation and reflection is critical to VBB's efficacy. The theory organises contexts (examiner disposition, panel credibility, timing, video number) around mechanisms (comparison, dissonance, schema adjustment) and outcomes (alignment of subsequent judgements).
requirements: Examiners must engage cognitively with both video observation and reflection on comparisons with their own scoring for the theory's alignment mechanism to operate
constraints: Derived from a single institution, a single history-taking station, and volunteer examiners; the authors state results may not generalise to other station types and that social/sociological contexts were not examined
target_learners: OSCE examiners (faculty) in medical education, experienced and novice
target_learning_goals: Alignment of examiners' scoring judgements to a shared standard in OSCEs
examples: The study manipulated benchmark performance level (borderline vs good) and timing of benchmark information (before vs after viewing) across 16 examiners and refined the initial programme theory into 13 CMOCs
key_sources: Edwards, R. J., Yeates, P., Lefroy, J., & McKinley, R. (2025). Understanding contexts and mechanisms through which video based benchmarking promotes alignment of examiners' scoring in objective structured clinical exams. Advances in Health Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-025-10454-3
